findings.condition: The stated criterion requires a fitted resistive DC path connecting /IN to /OUT, with no conduction assumed through unpopulated footprints and no alternate assembly override. In the saved design the only element between net /IN and net /OUT is R1 (10k, R_0805), and R1 is marked do-not-populate in both the schematic and the board.

findings.location: inputs/project/rc_filter.kicad_pcb:304 (R1 footprint, attr smd dnp) and inputs/project/rc_filter.kicad_sch:1261 (R1 dnp yes)
findings.mechanism: With R1 unpopulated, independent connectivity analysis of the saved board shows three disjoint DC islands, each net-pure: /IN (J1 pad 1, track ae12bf6f, R1 pad 1), /OUT (J1 pad 2, R1 pad 2, C1 pad 1, tracks 8b528360/a6dab0b4/69a2edc1), and GND. The only span between the /IN and /OUT islands is the absent R1 body across a 0.8 mm copper gap between R1 pad inner edges (x=104.6 to x=105.4 at y=100). J1 pin 1 to J1 pin 2 is therefore an open circuit as assembled; the fitted C1 is DC-open and provides no path. The copper routing is otherwise complete (bridging R1's pads joins the islands), so the failure is purely the population state.
findings.reasoning: The requirement is explicit and the native files are unambiguous: both the schematic symbol and the board footprint for R1 carry the DNP attribute, and no alternate assembly override exists. My pcbnew-based analysis modeled only fitted conductors (fitted resistors bridge their pads; fitted capacitors are DC-open; DNP footprints conduct nothing) and corrected for a mid-segment track T-junction at (107.5,100) so the /OUT copper is fully merged; even so, /IN remains isolated. Zero-violation ERC/DRC exits do not contradict this because KiCad connectivity treats DNP pads as net members; a successful tool exit is not proof of electrical behavior. This directly fails the sole evaluated criterion, hence blocking.
findings.title: No fitted resistive DC path from /IN to /OUT: series resistor R1 is DNP, leaving an open circuit in the saved assembly

findings.condition: The packet's four checks all report pass/info with zero violations on a board whose fitted assembly fails the stated /IN-to-/OUT requirement. ERC has no rule that a DNP part breaks a required path; DRC connectivity and schematic parity treat the DNP footprint's pads as valid net members (and dnp is set consistently in both files, so parity sees no mismatch); netlist and geometry merely record dnp as information without evaluating the fitted path.

findings.mechanism: A reviewer or gate relying on these green results would conclude the design is sound. The open circuit between J1 pin 1 and pin 2 in the saved assembly is only revealed by a population-aware connectivity analysis, which no packet check performs.
findings.reasoning: This is not a tool failure: each check executed correctly and reports what it measures. The concern is that the check suite's stimuli do not cover the packet's own acceptance criterion, so successful exits give false confidence. Flagged as a minor concern against verification coverage rather than a design defect; the underlying design failure is reported separately as PHY-1.
findings.title: Verification coverage gap: all packet checks pass while the sole functional criterion fails, because no check is assembly-population-aware

limitations: No SPICE/ngspice simulation performed; the failure is a topological open circuit and the packet defines no stimulus, so simulation would add no evidence
